Wrote scratchpad/cil_decode.mjs: a from-scratch ECMA-335 CIL disassembler (1-byte and 0xFE-prefixed 2-byte opcode tables, operand decoding, switch-target resolution) to decode the exact instruction stream of each of the 8 method bodies directly from the target's raw file bytes, using REA-reported file_offset/il_size as the starting point.
First decode pass on all 8 methods using file_offset directly as the CIL start. Output was garbled/inconsistent with REA's anchors.

Dumped raw hex bytes at each method's file_offset and cross-checked against REA-reported max_stack/il_size/local_var_sig_token. Determined file_offset points to the START OF THE METHOD HEADER (tiny=1 byte or fat=12 bytes), not the first CIL byte -- contradicting a literal reading of the task hint text, but confirmed unambiguously: the fat header's embedded CodeSize/MaxStack/LocalVarSigTok fields at that offset matched REA's il_size/max_stack/local_var_sig_token exactly for every method checked.
Fixed cil_decode.mjs to detect tiny vs fat method headers by the low 2 bits of the first byte and skip the correct header length before decoding CIL.

Re-ran decode on all 8 methods. m_4e09ee408f (M1), m_b2ece2c34c (M2), .cctor and m_5558f5ab53 (M8) now decoded cleanly and matched REA's curated anchors byte-offset-for-byte-offset. Main (m_ec38e2401a) still decoded garbage from IL_0000 (showed ldloc.0 where REA's anchors require ldarg.0).

Dumped Main's raw 16-byte fat header and recomputed by hand: flagsSize=0x301b. Recognized the bit layout was backwards in the script (it read the low 4 bits as header dword-size); per ECMA-335 II.25.4.3 the HIGH 4 bits of the 16-bit LE word are the dword-size (must be 3) and the LOW 12 bits are Flags. The bug was invisible on the other 7 methods only because none of them had CorILMethod_MoreSects (0x8) set, which is the only flag bit that collides with the (buggy) low-nibble read; Main has MoreSects set (it has a try/catch) so flagsSize&0xF produced 11 instead of 3, corrupting the CIL start offset by 32 bytes.
Fixed the fat-header size field to dwordSize = (flagsSize >>> 12) & 0xF.
Re-ran decode on Main. Header offset now correct, but a run of 'unk.dd'/garbage opcodes appeared starting around the try/catch region (leave/ldtoken/conv.u2 area).

Compared against .cctor's known ldtoken call (field 0x04000001, per REA anchor) and m_5558f5ab53's known conv.u2 usage, and found the single-byte opcode table had 0xC7..0xD7 mapped to the wrong mnemonics (shifted by 9 relative to the real ECMA-335 values: real ldtoken=0xD0 not 0xC7, real conv.u2=0xD1, leave=0xDD not 0xD4, leave.s=0xDE not 0xD5, etc.). This had not caused visible corruption in the other methods because the mis-mapped opcodes all happened to have the same (zero) operand length as their correct counterparts in those methods, so only the printed mnemonic was wrong there, not the byte alignment -- except in the two places (Main's leave/try-catch, and visually in m8's single conv.u2) where it mattered for readability.
Corrected the 0xC2-0xE0 single-byte opcode range to the real ECMA-335 mapping (ldtoken=0xD0, conv.u2=0xD1, conv.u1=0xD2, ..., leave=0xDD, leave.s=0xDE, stind.i=0xDF, conv.u=0xE0).

Re-ran decode on all 8 methods with the corrected table. All 8 now decode cleanly; cross-checked every REA-provided curated anchor (opcode name, IL offset, operand) for every method against this independent decode -- all matched exactly, including branch/switch targets and instruction_count totals.

Derived full semantics of M1 (ClampByte), M2 (AdjustChannel: (pixel-128)*contrast/100 trunc + 128 + brightness, then clamp), M3 (ApplyPreset: mono/warm/identity), M4 (Fnv: FNV-1a over int32 array elements), M5 (ParseIntInRange via real Int32.TryParse+range check, throws on failure), M6 (Main: --help fast path; arg-count/parse/range/preset validation wrapped in try/catch(ArgumentException); success path calls M2 x3, M3, M4, formats '{0},{1},{2}|{3:X8}'); M7 (.cctor: builds the byte[] string table from FieldRVA data via RuntimeHelpers.InitializeArray); M8 (DecodeString: XOR-decodes a byte range of the table with a single-byte key into a char[], then String(char[])).

Brute-forced the file offset of the 235-byte FieldRVA string-table blob by XOR-decoding all 11 distinct (offset,length,key) triples found across the 8 method bodies at candidate base offsets 2500-2506 and scoring how many decoded to fully printable ASCII. base=2504 scored 11/11 with clean English text (e.g. 'mono', 'warm', 'integer out of range', '--help', 'PixelTone R G B brightness contrast preset', the usage detail line, 'expected 6 arguments; use --help', 'neutral', 'unknown preset', the composite format string, 'ERROR: '); every other candidate base scored <=6 and produced partial garbage. Treated this as conclusive identification of both the blob location and every decoded literal string used by the program.

detail: argv=["\u00a0100","0","0","0","100","neutral"] (literal U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE before the digits of the first numeric argument, all other args valid); purpose: the task's specifically-requested test of whether the target's int parser treats non-ASCII whitespace (NBSP) as trimmable before digits.
result: exit 2; stderr = 'ERROR: integer out of range\r\n' -- i.e. the NBSP was NOT trimmed and caused parse failure. argv_codepoints confirms the harness genuinely delivered U+00A0 as the first character, ruling out shell-level mangling. This resolves the ambiguity the task flagged: this binary's Int32.TryParse(..., NumberStyles.Integer, InvariantCulture) uses the narrow ASCII-only whitespace definition (U+0009-U+000D, U+0020), not a generic Unicode-whitespace trim.
